content.text: {"what_it_is":{"claims":[{"text":"Maritime Systems is a research and development program run by U.S. Special Operations Command (SOCOM) whose mission is the Engineering and Manufacturing Development of Special Operations Forces (SOF) surface and undersea mobility platforms — combatant craft and combat submersibles.","citation":{"fact_id":"d3d775a0ac98d2cf"}},{"text":"The program is funded through the Research, Development, Test and Evaluation, Defense-Wide account.","citation":{"fact_id":"913b275e47c4e9ef"}},{"text":"The program is organized into two main projects: Underwater Systems (project number S0417) and Surface Craft (project number S1684).","citation":{"fact_id":"3561bab5def52110"}},{"text":"The Underwater Systems project covers development of combat submersibles, SOF combat diving systems, underwater support systems, and underwater equipment used for infiltration/extraction, personnel/material recovery, reconnaissance, and other missions.","citation":{"fact_id":"347942734768925a"}},{"text":"The Surface Craft project covers development of all combatant craft, combatant craft mission equipment, product improvements, and technology insertions to meet the unique requirements of SOF.","citation":{"fact_id":"3bdb993f363a2e89"}},{"text":"One underwater effort is the Dry Combat Submersible (DCS), a surface-launched, dry, atmosphere-controlled vessel that can insert and extract SOF personnel and their equipment into denied areas; SOCOM tested one submersible prototype to validate test methods and safety certification.","citation":{"fact_id":"494151bc4a1b7631"}},{"text":"Another underwater effort is the Sea, Air, and Land (SEAL) Delivery Vehicle (SDV) MK 11, a free-flooding combat submersible being developed to replace the legacy MK 8 MOD 1 system, with one Engineering Development Model and ten production units planned.","citation":{"fact_id":"58cfa8a0bbc566e3"}},{"text":"Surface efforts include the Combatant Craft Medium (CCM), a semi-enclosed multi-mission craft with a 40-knot speed, 600-nautical-mile range, and capacity for 4 crew plus 19 passengers, described as Naval Special Warfare's craft-of-choice for long-range, high-payload operations.","citation":{"fact_id":"50f89b017995c090"}},{"text":"Another surface craft, the Combatant Craft Assault (CCA), is a 41-foot combatant craft for squad-size operations with a 40-knot speed and 300-nautical-mile range that is transportable by C-130, C-17, or C-5 aircraft.","citation":{"fact_id":"20d7eea9cc4e1dc7"}},{"text":"The program also includes the Special Operations Craft Riverine (SOCR), an aluminum-hull platform for short-range insertion of SOF in riverine and littoral areas.","citation":{"fact_id":"d65d2f120fdd1663"}},{"text":"Newer development includes the Small Unmanned Surface Vehicle (SUSV), which procures commercial-off-the-shelf modular systems for short-endurance and long-endurance unmanned maritime missions.","citation":{"fact_id":"ff6383ace5b2fefc"}}]},"why_it_matters":{"claims":[{"text":"For fiscal year 2024, the program had actual spending of about $158.9 million (shown as 158,929 in thousands of dollars).","citation":{"fact_id":"913b275e47c4e9ef"}},{"text":"For fiscal year 2025, the enacted funding was about $200.8 million (200,770 in thousands of dollars).","citation":{"fact_id":"bcf67fd6dab3849a"}},{"text":"The fiscal year 2026 total request is about $301.3 million (301,288 in thousands of dollars).","citation":{"fact_id":"1408ef3f94e55739"}},{"text":"The FY2026 total combines a discretionary request of about $120.5 million (120,475 in thousands) with a reconciliation (mandatory) request of about $180.8 million (180,813 in thousands).","citation":{"fact_id":"b8a7759142190b73"}},{"text":"The reconciliation portion of the FY2026 request is about $180.8 million (180,813 in thousands of dollars).","citation":{"fact_id":"226938e5fffb6b0f"}},{"text":"Funding rose by about $100.5 million from FY2025 to FY2026, a roughly 50% increase — a large year-over-year jump that signals a major expansion of the program.","citation":{"fact_id":"d25e2785b1614b54"}},{"text":"According to the program narrative, the FY2026 reconciliation funding is tied to Section 20009 (INDOPACOM Capabilities) of the Reconciliation Exhibit, reflecting priorities in the Indo-Pacific region.","citation":{"fact_id":"d3d775a0ac98d2cf"}},{"text":"The program narrative breaks FY2026 into $246.2 million unclassified and $55.0 million classified, showing that a portion of the work is not publicly detailed.","citation":{"fact_id":"d3d775a0ac98d2cf"}}]},"players":{"claims":[{"text":"The program is managed by U.S. Special Operations Command (SOCOM).","citation":{"fact_id":"913b275e47c4e9ef"}},{"text":"Lobbying filings by Lockheed Martin Corporation in 2025 referenced maritime-related issues in connection with HR 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, Title II.","citation":{"fact_id":"1de4f074700ded6d"}},{"text":"General Dynamics Corp filings in 2024 and 2025 reported lobbying that referenced maritime matters alongside FY24, FY25, and FY26 Defense Appropriations issues.","citation":{"fact_id":"015c4934668b444c"}},{"text":"A General Dynamics filing reported lobbying on issues related to the Maritime Administration and Ready Reserve Sealift recapitalization.","citation":{"fact_id":"0179bc5ba2506034"}},{"text":"BAE Systems Land & Armaments LP filings in 2025 and 2026 reported lobbying on issues relating to military vehicles, munitions, and maritime systems.","citation":{"fact_id":"32df116ff58f4da2"}},{"text":"L3Harris Technologies Inc filings in 2024 referenced maritime matters in connection with the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025.","citation":{"fact_id":"06e33e5604b46d4b"}},{"text":"Because these lobbying mentions are only correlational — a filing referenced maritime topics — they do not indicate that any company won work or influenced the program.","citation":{"fact_id":"1de4f074700ded6d"}}]},"recent_developments":{"claims":[]}}
